# AP-BAG-001 Staff Baggage Handling and Escalation

## 1. Purpose and Scope  
This policy establishes the procedures and responsibilities for the handling of checked baggage throughout the airport's baggage handling system. It applies to all staff involved in the movement, sorting, and loading of checked baggage between the check-in belts, the baggage make-up area, and the aircraft loading zones. The policy ensures that baggage is handled in a safe, efficient, and compliant manner, while maintaining the integrity of the airline's operations and passenger expectations. This document outlines the roles, responsibilities, and standards for baggage handling and defines the escalation procedures for baggage incidents to ensure timely and appropriate responses.

## 2. Roles and Responsibilities  
The Baggage Handler is responsible for the physical handling of checked baggage, including loading, unloading, and sorting. The Baggage Duty Supervisor oversees the activities of the Baggage Handlers and ensures compliance with all handling procedures and safety protocols. The Ramp Lead is responsible for coordinating the baggage handling operations with the aircraft loading and unloading teams. All staff must follow the procedures outlined in this policy and report any deviations or incidents in accordance with the escalation process. The Baggage Duty Supervisor is the primary point of contact for any baggage handling issues and is responsible for ensuring that all incidents are properly documented and escalated as required.

## 3. Handling Standards  
All baggage must be handled with care to prevent damage, loss, or misrouting. Baggage Handlers must inspect each bag for visible damage or abnormalities before handling and report any concerns to the Baggage Duty Supervisor. Heavy bags must be handled using proper lifting techniques to avoid injury, and all fragile items must be clearly marked and handled with extra caution. When loading baggage onto aircraft, handlers must ensure that all bags are properly secured and that the weight distribution is balanced. The Baggage Duty Supervisor is responsible for monitoring the handling process and ensuring that all baggage is processed in accordance with the airline's operational standards and safety regulations.

## 4. Baggage Incident Escalation  
When a baggage handler finds a damaged, leaking, or unattended checked bag in the baggage make-up area, the handler must escalate the incident to the Baggage Duty Supervisor within 10 minutes of discovery and must report it under AP-INC-002. All incidents must be documented in the incident log and reported to the Ramp Lead for further action. The Baggage Duty Supervisor is responsible for assessing the incident and determining the appropriate course of action, including notifying the relevant airline representatives if necessary. Any delay in reporting or escalating an incident may result in operational inefficiencies or safety risks. The Baggage Duty Supervisor must ensure that all incidents are resolved in a timely manner and that all affected parties are informed of the outcome.

## 5. Restricted Items Found in Baggage  
If a restricted item is found in a bag during the baggage handling process, the bag must not be further handled until it is approved or removed under the restricted-items approval procedure in AP-SEC-003. The Baggage Duty Supervisor is responsible for identifying and isolating the bag containing the restricted item and ensuring that it is not processed further. The bag must be secured and marked for inspection by the appropriate security personnel. All staff must be aware of the procedures outlined in AP-SEC-003 and must not attempt to handle or remove restricted items without proper authorization. The Baggage Duty Supervisor must coordinate with the security team to ensure that the restricted item is dealt with in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

## 6. Records and Review  
All baggage handling incidents must be recorded in the incident log, which is maintained by the Baggage Duty Supervisor. The log must include details such as the time of discovery, the nature of the incident, the actions taken, and the outcome. The incident log is reviewed annually by the airport management team to assess the effectiveness of the baggage handling procedures and to identify any areas for improvement. The Baggage Duty Supervisor is responsible for ensuring that the log is updated regularly and that all entries are accurate and complete. The airport management team will conduct a review of this policy at least once per year to ensure that it remains current and effective in addressing the needs of the baggage handling operations.
